stemMd: A nominal annual interest rate is 5% and prices rise by 3% over the same year. What is the approximate real interest rate using the usual subtraction approximation?
explanationMd: The usual approximation subtracts inflation from nominal interest: five minus three gives two percent. The exact purchasing-power return is 1.05/1.03 minus one, about 1.94%. The question explicitly requests the approximation.

distractorRationale.a: This adds inflation rather than subtracting it.
distractorRationale.e: This ignores the loss of purchasing power.
distractorRationale.d: Multiplication of the two percentages does not give the real rate.
